title: Headings
definition: HTML elements `<h1>` through `<h6>` used to define the headings of a page, representing a hierarchy of importance.
simpleExplanation: Headings are the titles and subtitles of your webpage, exactly like an outline for an essay. `<h1>` is the main title of the page (you should only have one!). `<h2>` are the major sections, and `<h3>` are subsections within those.
realWorldExample: A news article. The headline is `<h1>`. The main sections of the article are `<h2>`. If a section has bullet points with titles, those are `<h3>`.
useCases: SEO (Google reads headings to understand the page)

basic: Which heading tag is the largest and most important?
intermediate: Why shouldn't you use an `<h2>` just to make text bold and big?

answers.question: Why not use it just for styling?
answers.answer: Headings are for STRUCTURE, not style. Blind users use screen readers to jump from heading to heading to navigate the page. If you use an `<h2>` randomly in a paragraph just because it looks big, you destroy the structural map of the page. Use CSS (`font-size`, `font-weight`) to make text big.
